draft.title: Proofs about numbers
card: Divisibility proofs use algebra. An even number is 2m and an odd number is 2m + 1, where m is a whole number.
Example: the sum of two odd numbers is even. (2a + 1) + (2b + 1) = 2a + 2b + 2 = 2(a + b + 1), which is a multiple of 2.
Inequalities can be proved by rearranging. To show a² + b² ≥ 2ab, note that a² + b² − 2ab = (a − b)², which is never negative.
To show √2 is irrational, assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms. Then p² = 2q², so p and q are both even. This contradicts lowest terms.
draft.remember: Write numbers in algebraic form, then rearrange to show the property.

a.q: Which expression shows the product of two consecutive whole numbers is always even?
opts: n(n + 1), because one of n and n + 1 is even
n(n + 2), because n + 2 is always even
n(n + 1), because n and n + 1 are both odd
2n, because it is a multiple of 2
a.why: Of two consecutive whole numbers, one is even, so the product has a factor of 2. In n(n + 2), n and n + 2 are both odd when n is odd, so that product is not always even.
a.clue: Consecutive numbers alternate between even and odd.

b.q: Which line correctly completes a proof that a² + b² ≥ 2ab for all real a and b?
opts: a² + b² − 2ab = (a − b)² ≥ 0
a² + b² − 2ab = (a + b)² ≥ 0
a² + b² − 2ab = a² − b² ≥ 0
a² + b² − 2ab = 2(a − b) ≥ 0
b.why: Expanding (a − b)² gives a² − 2ab + b², which matches. A square is never negative, so the inequality holds. (a + b)² expands to a² + 2ab + b², which has the wrong sign on 2ab.
b.clue: Expand each bracket and compare with a² − 2ab + b².

a.best: n(n + 1), because one of n and n + 1 is even

problems.detail: The √2 proof jumps from p² = 2q² to 'p and q are both even'. The missing steps are that p² is even so p is even, then p = 2k gives q² = 2k², so q is even. As written, it looks as if both follow at once, which could confuse students.

check.summary: Both questions have exactly one correct answer, and the explanations agree with them. The card's √2 proof skips the step showing why p, and then q, must be even, so it should be expanded.

proposal.title: Proofs about numbers
card: Divisibility proofs use algebra. Write an even number as 2m and an odd number as 2m + 1, where m is a whole number. Of two consecutive numbers, n and n + 1, one is even and one is odd.
Example: the sum of two odd numbers is even. (2a + 1) + (2b + 1) = 2a + 2b + 2 = 2(a + b + 1), which is a multiple of 2.

To show √2 is irrational, assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms. Then p² = 2q² is even, so p is even. Putting p = 2k gives 4k² = 2q², so q² = 2k² and q is even too, which breaks lowest terms.
